accepted_gaps.title: Typed future is not operationalized
accepted_gaps.statement: Deterministic trajectory prediction, probabilistic forecasting, and conditional scenario projection are often discussed together, preventing comparable claims.

accepted_gaps.title: Forecastability has no common horizon scale
accepted_gaps.statement: Lead time is meaningful only relative to system timescales, but cross-domain benchmarks rarely normalize horizon by intrinsic dynamics.

accepted_gaps.title: Uncertainty components are confounded
accepted_gaps.statement: Initial-state, observation, model, process, and distribution-shift uncertainty are not consistently separated in AI forecast comparisons.

accepted_gaps.title: Skill is reported more often than calibration
accepted_gaps.statement: Point accuracy or average rank is insufficient for decisions that require reliable probabilities and tail-event behavior.

accepted_gaps.title: AI gains may be domain-specific
accepted_gaps.statement: Modern learned weather models show substantial bounded gains, but transfer across regimes and other complex systems remains unresolved.

accepted_gaps.title: Computational speed is not information
accepted_gaps.statement: Faster inference or larger models can improve access to forecasts without creating information about an unobserved or chaotic future.

accepted_gaps.title: Decision usefulness is rarely tested with forecastability
accepted_gaps.statement: A forecast can be statistically skillful yet poorly calibrated or badly timed for an operational decision.
